newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt partially reverses credit freeze.
newsitem.headline: French govt partially reverses credit freeze.

text.p: France's Socialist-led government said on Wednesday it had decided to reverse only partially a 10-billion franc ($1.7 billion) freeze on credit lines made by the previous centre-right administration.
The last government announced the spending freeze in March to ensure it could reduce the public deficit to 3.0 percent of gross domestic product this year.
Finance Ministry documents said the government's new spending measures planned would be financed by releasing some of the money frozen in March.
Of eight billion francs in credit lines in the civil budget frozen in March, 2.5 billion will be redeployed to fund justice, housing, education and research.
The 1.8 billion francs in the military budget frozen in March would be completely scrapped, the documents said.
The rest of the new spending measures, costing a total 11.1 billion francs, would be funded by scrapping spending planned elsewhere or by reallocating spending from one area to another.

Plans to create 40,000 to 70,000 jobs for example, at a cost of two billion francs, will be funded by a surplus in the 150 billion franc budget set aside to finance job creation schemes introduced by the previous government.
